searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase one — boundless social network brainstorm the awtsmoos renews every voice before a timeline learns its name; awtsmoos.com should reveal a social world where depth expands by choice, never by cluttered frame. north star transform the current social observatory plus interaction studio into one coherent social network experience. the default layer should feel human, fast, calm, mobile first, and socially alive. exact api routes, payloads, json, health probes, schemas, and developer evidence remain available through retractable advanced surfaces rather than occupying the primary experience. product universe 1. home feed with readable social cards instead of raw json. 2. discover surface for people, heichelos, series, posts, comments, and recommendations. 3. profile surface with identity, activity, graph, analytics, history, relationships, roles, and references. 4. communities / heichelos surface with membership, editors, submissions, moderation, posts, series, and governance. 5. composer surface for posts, questions, comments, replies, media, canonical references, and provenance aware promotion. 6. notifications / signals with unread state, human summaries, actions, and read management where backend support exists. 7. relationships with following, followers, recommendations, graph context, and deliberate follow mutations. 8. activity / privacy with user visible history, reading continuity, activity ledger, retention, and supported privacy controls. 9. moderation / review with submissions, editors, review center, governance evidence, and permission aware mutation controls. 10. live social current with replay, presence, subscriptions, and publishing in an explicit live chamber. 11. messaging / communications surfaced only from verified existing backend capabilities, without guessing what the unfinished user phrase “add m” meant. 12. developer chamber with openapi, route health, key verification, cache probes, exact requests, responses, and capability parity. ux universe 13. one mobile first shell with a compact bottom/top navigation model and optional desktop rail. 14. primary navigation names tasks rather than backend nouns: home, discover, create, profile, inbox, more. 15. advanced surfaces use native where possible and bounded drawers only when focus lifecycle requires them. 16. every rich card has a concise summary, contextual actions, and optional exact data disclosure. 17. composer is retractable and contextual: opening it from a post/comment/profile carries target context automatically. 18. permission dependent controls render disabled/hidden with an explanation rather than failing after a click. 19. empty states teach the next useful action. 20. loading states are skeletons or compact progress states, never giant blank cards. 21. error states translate structured backend errors into human next steps while preserving raw evidence under advanced. 22. infinite or paginated lists use explicit load more or intersection behavior with abortable requests and stable focus. 23. navigation state is url addressable so social surfaces can be shared/bookmarked. 24. on mobile, secondary rail/navigation retracts completely and never overlays content accidentally. 25. no fixed surface uses raw viewport width; all sheets use inset safe inline sizing and max block height. 26. no uncontrolled z index escalation; local layers are named and bounded. 27. pointer hover is progressive enhancement inside hover capable media queries. 28. touch active states and keyboard focus visible states exist independently. 29. reduced motion preserves state meaning. 30. long aliases, ids, urls, code, media, and json never widen the page. api / architecture universe 31. split the current hub/api.js monolith into a tiny transport plus domain endpoint modules. 32. keep a stable socialapi facade so callers do not break during internal modularization. 33. introduce a data driven capability registry that records key, group, mode, label, endpoint family, required context, danger level, and presentation adapter. 34. registry parity should be testable against the backend’s supported public capability contract. 35. unknown or undocumented mutations are never auto exposed as executable controls. 36. read capabilities may be discoverable dynamically, but presentation adapters remain explicit for human quality output. 37. mutation policy stays explicit and consequence labeled. 38. request construction remains isolated from rendering and state. 39. human renderers map common response shapes into feed/profile/relationship/notification/community cards. 40. exact request and response evidence lives in reusable advanced disclosure components. 41. existing /social hub/ canonical interaction logic should be reused or linked contextually rather than reimplemented in parallel. 42. existing social backend modules remain authoritative for behavior and authorization. 43. frontend never bypasses server permission checks. 44. new code uses tabs, descriptive torah/kabbalah inspired internal names, exhaustive jsdoc, and small files. 45. public ui labels remain simple and predictable. backend parity universe the live router actively composes identity, communications, civilization, objects, aliases, keys, graph, search, content, community, entities, living state, thoughts, assets, drive, editor, governance, notifications, packed data, platform, migrations, heichelos, posts, counters, mail, filesystem, nodeos, comments, series, books, plus social kernel/profile/discovery/summary layers. the frontend must create a discoverable path for every supported public capability, but administrative/internal operations must remain permission aware and never become unauthenticated power buttons merely because a route exists. documentation universe 46. social documentation becomes an actual product map rather than a paragraph. 47. every social chamber documents user purpose, backend capability family, required identity/context, mutations, and advanced evidence path. 48. developer docs include exact api quickstarts and capability discovery. 49. architecture docs explain observatory vs interaction studio consolidation and reuse boundaries. 50. a parity report records backend capabilities that have full ui, advanced only ui, or intentionally non public status. verification universe 51. static scope audit: every social hub css selector must remain route/component local. 52. interaction audit: hover/active/focus visible/disabled/busy/expanded states. 53. layout audit at 320, 390, 768, and desktop widths. 54. keyboard only navigation across rail, tabs, cards, disclosures, composer, and dialogs. 55. console cleanliness and failed network handling. 56. capability parity test between frontend registry and verified public backend surface. 57. api facade tests for each endpoint family. 58. mutation boundary tests to ensure reads cannot secretly mutate. 59. raw evidence disclosure tests for developer access. 60. complete file readback and planned vs actual delta before completion. architectural restraint the social network should not become one giant page or one giant api object. the awtsmoos is revealed through many bounded keilim: small modules, clear ownership, one source of truth, predictable public names, and advanced power that unfolds only when requested.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase two — architecture and capability parity the awtsmoos gives every social force a vessel, and every vessel a measured shore; awtsmoos.com should reveal the whole network through one clear door, with deeper truth unfolding only when users ask for more. evidence /social/ is a capable but developer shaped observatory. /social hub/ is already the richer human product with inbox, dms, live chat, people, spaces, network, profile, activity, privacy, creation, canonical comments/replies, media, promotion, references, review, and governance. the live /api/social router composes far more backend families than /social/ currently exposes. social hub/js/api/ already has domain apis for graph, activity, channels, communications, destinations, governance, interactions, reviews, and transport. social hub/style.css already composes many route local modules; creating another global styling layer would be architectural regression. social hub/index.html is a remaining monolith. new ui should not be appended inline. chosen architecture product center /social hub/ is the human social network. /social/ becomes the developer/capability observatory and explicit doorway into the human product. do not duplicate inbox, messages, chat, community, profile, or interaction logic between them. capability model create a small data registry under social hub/js/capabilities/ describing supported user facing capabilities. each record contains: id label group mode: read / mutation / navigation required identity/context implementation status route/panel destination advanced api evidence link where applicable the registry is presentation metadata, not authorization. the server remains authoritative. capability center ui create a runtime generated, retractable capability center instead of adding another giant section to index.html. it should: summarize available social powers in human language; route users to the existing owning panel; show missing context requirements; expose raw api/openapi details only inside advanced; make communications, publishing, comments, reactions, communities, governance, activity, profile, graph, discovery, and developer tooling discoverable from one place. observatory bridge upgrade /social/ so its primary cta opens the social hub and its developer cards link back to the human surface that owns each capability. preserve raw observatory probes for agents/developers. api cleanup do not rewrite the already modular social hub/js/api foundation. the technical debt target is the separate scripts/awtsmoos/social/hub/api.js observatory monolith. split it into transport plus small domain groups while preserving the socialapi facade. css new social hub styles must be imported from social hub/style.css and every selector must begin beneath .social hub document or a dedicated component root that itself lives beneath that route. no naked element/root selectors. no 100vw. no arbitrary z index. suggested new modules: styles/capability center.css styles/capability disclosure.css styles/social polish.css do not create these if existing style modules already own the same concern; reuse first. verification graph 1. source structure and line count checks. 2. social hub style ownership test. 3. api foundation tests. 4. communications/governance/interaction tests. 5. capability registry coverage test. 6. mobile route visibility test. 7. browser smoke at 390px and desktop. 8. horizontal overflow probe. 9. keyboard route/disclosure/focus restoration probe. 10. console error ledger. 11. full touched file reread. 12. planned vs actual delta. files that may be touched after final critique new geelooy/social hub/js/capabilities/ new geelooy/social hub/js/ui/capabilitycenter.js or similarly small view/controller split geelooy/social hub/js/appassembly.js only if needed to assemble the new capability controller geelooy/social hub/js/hubapp.js only if lifecycle integration cannot remain inside assembly geelooy/social hub/style.css import manifest new localized social hub css modules geelooy/social/documentation.md geelooy/social hub/documentation.md observatory api modules under geelooy/scripts/awtsmoos/social/hub/api/ plus compatibility api.js parity/structure tests protected areas do not rewrite the large social hub html unless a later decomposition mission first extracts existing panels into smaller owned templates. do not duplicate messages/chat/inbox logic. do not expose privileged backend mutations without existing authorization semantics and explicit consequence ui.
